newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's oil imports dip slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan's oil imports dip slightly in 1996.

text.p: Japan's crude oil imports in 1996 fell for the second year in a row, dipping 1.3 percent to 263.5 million kilolitres (kl), the trade ministry said on Tuesday.
The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said the Middle East was the source for 80 percent of Japan's crude imports last year, up slightly from 78.6 percent in 1995.
The top three exporters of crude oil to Japan in 1996 were the United Arab Emirates at 27 percent, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19.8 percent and Iran at 9.9 percent.
Imports from the United Arab Emirates declined 1.1 percent to 71.1 million kl, while Saudi Arabia inched up 0.6 percent to 52.3 million kl.
Shipments from Iran showed a marked increase of 13.3 percent to 26 million kl, although a MITI official said the rise largely reflected the fact imports from Iran had been particularly low in 1995.
"Crude oil imports from Iran in 1996 returned to the levels of two years ago," he said.
Japan processed a total of 243.7 million kl of crude in 1996, up from 242.9 million kl the previous year.
Following a U.N. oil-for-food deal, Japanese oil companies last year signed an agreement to purchase a total of 20,000 barrels per day of crude oil from Iraq over a six-month period.
The first shipments are due to arrive in Japan in mid-February. They will be the first imports from Iraq since sanctions were imposed against Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of neighbouring Kuwait.
Imports from Asia, excluding China, amounted to 30.6 million kl in 1996, or 11.6 percent of all imports.
Indonesia shipped a total of 18.0 million kl of crude oil in 1996, compared with 21.0 million kl in 1995.
It nevertheless remained the largest source of Asian crude oil for Japan in 1996.
China exported a total of 13.2 million kl of crude oil in 1996, or five percent of Japan's total imports. In 1995, the volume was 13.6 million kl.

In December, Japan imported a total of 23.1 million kl of crude oil, up 0.6 percent from the same month a year earlier. It was the second consecutive month in which crude imports had increased on a year-on-year basis.
The United Arab Emirates was the top exporter of crude oil to Japan last month, accounting for some 6.0 million kl, though the volume was down 4.3 percent from December 1995.
The second-largest source of exports to Japan in December was Saudi Arabia at 5.7 million kl, followed by Iran at 2.3 million kl.
